statement_record.book: In the topos of sheaves on a space X, a predicate on a sheaf S is a sheaf morphism p : S → Ω into the subobject classifier; by the definition of a sheaf morphism it gives, for each open U, a function S(U) → Ω(U), so p applied to a section s over U returns an open subset of U — the region of U on which the predicate holds of s.
statement_record.intree: Class SubobjectClassifier := { Ω : C; truth : 1 ~> Ω; char {u x} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω; char_pullback ... : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one; char_unique ... } together with Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the general topos content — a predicate on x is exactly an element of the hom-setoid x ~> Ω, and classifier_classifies asserts these correspond bijectively (as setoids) to subobjects of x; intree-weaker in instantiation: the correspondence is available only for FinSet (Ω = 2, Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v) and as cross-universe theorems for Sets (Instance/Sets/Classifier.v), never for a sheaf topos, so the book's defining unwinding — a predicate assigns to a section over U an OPEN SUBSET of U — has no in-tree instance.

statement_record.book: A predicate p : S → Ω determines, by subobject classification, a subobject of S written {s in S | p(s)} (the comprehension of S along p); describe the sections of that subsheaf over an arbitrary open U.
statement_record.intree: `sub_reindex h truth_subobject` is the comprehension of a predicate h : x ~> Ω (the pullback of the generic subobject truth along h), and the two round trips assert it is inverse to classification: classifier_char_roundtrip : char (sub_mono (sub_reindex h truth_subobject)) ... ≈ h, and classifier_pullback_roundtrip : sub_reindex (char (sub_mono s) (sub_is_monic s)) truth_subobject ≈ s. In the FinSet topos the comprehension is computed: fin_select_sat asserts every member of the cut-out subset fin_countP P satisfies P (with fin_select_rank giving the converse).

statement_record.book: Pred_S := (Hom_{Sh(X)}(S, Ω), ≤), where p ≤ q iff for every open U and every section s ∈ S(U) the open p(s) is contained in q(s) (also written p ⊢ q). The relation is antisymmetric — mutual containment of opens is equality — so this is a genuine partial order; when S = 1 its elements are called propositions, i.e. morphisms 1 → Ω.
statement_record.intree: Definition sub_le (u v : SubObj x) : Type := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }, with sub_le_refl / sub_le_trans, and Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u); Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) in Sets.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in placement, same in content on the subobject side: the entailment order is defined on SubObj x (factorization of monos), where sub_equiv_iff_mutual is exactly the book's antisymmetry (mutual entailment = equality in the quotient) and sub_le_refl/sub_le_trans make it a preorder. The identification of predicates with subobjects (classifier_classifies) is an isomorphism of SETOIDS ONLY — the order is never transported across it, so the hom-setoid x ~> Ω carries no in-tree order relation, and 'Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets' (Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:180) lands in Sets rather than in a category of posets.

gap: Three precise gaps. (1) No order is defined on the object of predicates: `sub_le` lives on SubObj x, and nothing in-tree defines p ≤ q for p q : x ~> Ω, nor transports sub_le along classifier_classifies (which is only an iso of setoids; grep shows `sub_le` has ZERO uses outside Theory/Subobject.v). statement_record.book: All the logical symbols of §7.4.2 (⊤, ⊥, ∧, ∨, ⇒, ¬) extend to predicates on any sheaf S by computing pointwise — (p ∧ q)(s) := p(s) ∧ q(s), etc. With respect to the order of (7.63), ∧ is the meet and ∨ the join in the sense of Chapter 1; and the poset of predicates on S is a Heyting algebra (the term is not defined, deferred to further reading).
statement_record.intree: Props is the thin category of propositions ordered by implication, equipped with Props_Terminal (⊤ = True), Props_Initial (⊥ = False), Props_Cartesian (∧ = product = meet), Props_Cocartesian (∨ = coproduct = join) and Props_Closed (⇒ = exponential, via the currying iso Hom(R ∧ P, Q) ≅ Hom(R, P → Q)) — i.e. a bicartesian closed thin category, which is exactly a Heyting prealgebra.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on carrier and on pointwise-ness. What is proved is that the TRUTH VALUES themselves (Prop, ordered by implication) form a Heyting prealgebra — the S = 1 case of the book's claim, and in the Set-like setting only. Nothing asserts that predicates on a general object S, i.e. the hom-setoid S ~> Ω or SubObj S in a topos, carry any of these operations; there is no Heyting-algebra CLASS in the library (Props is an instance of Cartesian/Cocartesian/Closed, not of a named Heyting structure), and the pointwise extension of connectives from Ω to predicates is nowhere performed. Negation ¬p = (p ⇒ ⊥) is derivable from Props_Closed + Props_Initial but is not stated.

gap: The Heyting structure is proved only on the truth-value poset Props (Prop with implication), never on Pred(S) = (S ~> Ω) or on SubObj S.
